A vaccine is a biological product which induces immunity against a particular disease by inoculating agent(s) that resemble a disease-causing microorganism(s) and is often made from weakened pathogens, its toxins or one of the surface proteins.
A vaccination is the process of injection of a killed or weakened organism or its components like toxins or surface proteins that produce specific immunity in the body against that organism.

1. INACTIVATED VACCINE (Killed Vaccine) Consists of pathogen(s) which are inactivated or killed by physical or chemical methods so that organisms totally lose their pathogenicity and virulence.
2. LIVE VACCINES Contain live organisms that cause diseases, modified either in nature or in laboratory so that they lose ability to cause disease but retain ability to elicit immune response in the body.
3. RECOMBINANT VACCINES Made using recombinant DNA technology. Have characteristics of inactivated or attenuated vaccines and generally consist of expressed proteins.

✓ Protects animals against particular diseases ✓ Prevents epidemics and pandemics of diseases ✓ Prevents spread of communicable diseases to other animals and humans ✓ Prevents cost incurred in treatment of infected animals ✓ Prevents certain animal diseases having food borne spread potential ✓ Ensures herd health and productivity

1. Only healthy animals should be vaccinated. Weak, pregnant, or immuno-compromised animals should NOT be vaccinated.
2. Deworming before vaccination is always preferred for effective vaccination.
3. Vaccination should be done at least 20-30 days before probable time of disease spread.
4. Vaccination should be done with vaccine maintained under proper cold chain.
5. All animals in a herd should be vaccinated to achieve desired level of herd immunity.
6. Avoid vaccination in the last trimester of pregnancy.
7. Always maintain animal health card to record vaccination history.
8. Use separate syringe and needle for each animal. Safely dispose used needles and syringes.
9. Vaccinate during cool parts of the day (early morning/late evening).
10. Do not vaccinate animals under stress (transport, market, extreme weather).

1. IMPROPER ADMINISTRATION Vaccination not done at appropriate time, dose, and route.
2. IMPROPER MIXING OF VACCINES Vaccine not properly mixed before use.
3. IMPROPER STORAGE Vaccine effectiveness reduces if not stored at temperature specified by manufacturer.
4. POOR QUALITY OF VACCINE Sometimes poor quality vaccines may lead to vaccine failure.
5. IMPROPER TIMING Too early vaccination leads to maternal antibody interference. Too late vaccination may not be effective if disease already present.
6. ANIMAL FACTORS Environmental stress, poor nutrition, inappropriate age, and transportation stress may lead to vaccine failure.
7. LACK OF HERD IMMUNITY If majority of animals (less than 80%) in herd are not immunized, herd immunity reduces and vaccine failure may occur.

DISEASE: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) Causative Agent: PPR virus / Morbillivirus
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Live attenuated cell culture PPR vaccine (freeze-dried) Serotype: Sungri/96 strain
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 4 months old Number of doses: Single dose Duration of immunity: At least 3 years Route: Subcutaneous injection Booster: After 3 years only
SPECIAL NOTES - One of the most important vaccines for goats - Protects against highly contagious disease - Single lifetime dose provides long-lasting immunity

DISEASE: Sheep Pox Causative Agent: Sheep pox virus / Capripox virus
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Attenuated virus in freeze-dried vaccine Serotypes: Srinagar Strain, Romanian Fannar Strain, Ranipet strain
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 4 months and above Frequency: At least once a year Route: Subcutaneous injection Best time: Before disease season (Feb-March)
SPECIAL NOTES - FOR SHEEP ONLY (not for goats) - Annual vaccination recommended for complete protection - Important during cooler months when disease risk is higher

DISEASE: Goat Pox Causative Agent: Goat pox virus / Capripox virus
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Live attenuated cell culture Goat-Pox vaccine Serotype: Uttarkashi strain
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 4 months or older Frequency: Annual vaccination Route: Subcutaneous injection Timing: After kidding season or before breeding season
SPECIAL NOTES - FOR GOATS ONLY (not for sheep) - Protects against high mortality disease - Annual booster recommended for continued immunity

DISEASE: Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) Causative Agent: FMD virus / Apthovirus
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Inactivated tissue culture aluminium hydroxide gel adsorbed vaccine Inactivated tissue culture oil adjuvant vaccine Combined vaccines Serotypes: FMDV serotypes O, A, and Asia 1
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: First dose at 4 months old Primary course: First dose + booster at 2-4 weeks Frequency: Booster every 6 months Standard schedule: March and October Route: Intramuscular injection
SPECIAL NOTES - Requires regular boosters for continued immunity - Fixed schedule (March & October) follows India\'s vaccination calendar - Applies to both sheep and goats

DISEASE: Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) Causative Agent: Pasteurella multocida (Serotype B:2)
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Inactivated aluminium hydroxide gel adsorbed vaccine Inactivated alum precipitated vaccine Inactivated oil adjuvant vaccine Serotype: P. multocida P52
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 6 months and above Frequency: Annual vaccination Best time: Before monsoon (May-June) Route: Subcutaneous injection
SPECIAL NOTES - Pre-monsoon vaccination is crucial as disease spreads during rains - Annual booster provides one year of protection - Protects both sheep and goats - Part of important herd immunity program

DISEASE: Anthrax Causative Agent: Bacillus anthracis
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Anthrax live spore vaccine Serotypes: Bacillus anthracis Sterne strain (34 F₂)
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 6 months old Frequency: Annual vaccination Best time: Before monsoon (July-August) Dose: Not less than 5.0 million spores per dose Route: Subcutaneous injection
SPECIAL NOTES - Only recommended in Anthrax enzootic areas - In Karnataka: Priority zones are Chamarajanagar, Mandya, Mysuru districts - Annual booster essential in high-risk areas - More critical in these specific regions

DISEASE: Enterotoxaemia (ET) Causative Agent: Clostridium perfringens type D
VACCINE DETAILS Types: Formalin inactivated cultures with epsilon toxoid adjuvantated with aluminium hydroxide gel Serotype: Clostridium perfringens Type D
VACCINATION PROTOCOL Age to vaccinate: 4 months old (if dam vaccinated) OR 1 week old (if dam unvaccinated) Booster: 15 days after primary vaccination Annual booster: Before monsoon Route: Subcutaneous injection
SPECIAL NOTES - Dam\'s vaccination status determines starting age - Requires booster 15 days after primary dose - Annual vaccination recommended - Protects both sheep and goats - Important for young animals

❌ DO NOT VACCINATE IF:
1. ANIMAL IS ILL - Animal shows fever (temperature > 39°C) - Animal shows clinical signs of any disease - Animal appears weak or lethargic
2. ANIMAL IS PREGNANT - Avoid live vaccines in last trimester of pregnancy - Inactivated vaccines can be given with caution
3. ANIMAL IS MALNOURISHED - Poor nutritional status reduces vaccine effectiveness - Wait until animal recovers nutritionally
4. ANIMAL IS IMMUNOCOMPROMISED - Recent concurrent illness - Ongoing treatment that suppresses immunity
5. RECENT MEDICATION - Antiparasitic drugs: Wait 1 week before vaccination - Antibiotics: Avoid during vaccination period
6. STRESS CONDITIONS - After transport/market exposure - During extreme weather - During breeding/kidding season (except specific vaccines)
7. INADEQUATE COLD CHAIN - Vaccine shows signs of damage - Temperature exposure breaks cold chain - Never re-freeze a thawed vaccine
ALWAYS CONSULT LOCAL VETERINARIAN Contact your veterinary officer for specific advice on your animals.

ABOUT GRAMA-VAXI Version: 1.0 Release Date: 2026
Grama-Vaxi is a livestock health alert application designed to help farmers in rural Karnataka maintain vaccination records for their sheep and goats.
FEATURES ✓ Animal Health Card with vaccination tracking ✓ Automatic vaccine reminder notifications ✓ Government camp alert system ✓ Disease reporting to local veterinarians ✓ Comprehensive vaccination information ✓ Bilingual interface (English & Kannada)
MISSION To improve livestock health and prevent disease outbreaks in rural villages through timely vaccination reminders and health digitization.
